item.title: [Campaign: milestone] Plan for Windows Server 2016 and Windows 10 2016 LTSB end of support
item.description:
13 January 2027 as printed in this 60-day reminder; Microsoft's 90-day reminder MC1507705 printed 12 January 2027.

Next: 13 Jan 2027.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Out-of-band Windows update fixes SLMGR licensing and KMS activation failures (error 0x80041008) caused by the November 2026 security update
item.description:
Scripted KMS and product-key provisioning breaks on freshly built or re-imaged servers, so new hosts can come up unactivated; it is a reliability fault in the November patch, not a vulnerability.

Windows · If build or activation scripts call slmgr.vbs and failed after the November update, import the matching OOB KB from the Microsoft Update Catalog; no action for devices that are already activated.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 ends mainstream support on 13 January 2027 (60-day reminder) - the 90-day reminder MC1507706 said 12 January
item.description:
LTSC 2021 sits on kiosks, OT jump hosts and specialised devices that are easy to forget; without ESU they stop receiving security fixes after January 2027.

Windows · Inventory Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 devices and decide per device between Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024 and ESU before the January 2027 update.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Windows Server 2016 ends extended support on 13 January 2027 (60-day reminder) - the 90-day reminder MC1507705 said 12 January
item.description:
Unpatched Windows Server 2016 domain controllers, AD FS, AD CS or Entra Connect hosts become a permanent tier-0 exposure from February 2027 unless enrolled in ESU.

Windows Server · List every Windows Server 2016 host, starting with domain controllers and identity servers, and either migrate it or enrol it in ESU before the January 2027 update.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Since the October 2026 updates, domain controllers require LDAP Kerberos tickets to match the LDAP SPN; NetApp SMB shares with LDAP session security 'none' can fail
item.description:
A DC hardening that blocks tickets issued for other services from authenticating to LDAP; rolling it back to restore storage access reopens the hole it closes.

Windows Server · Find NetApp and Azure NetApp Files AD connections with LDAP session security 'none' and move them to sign or seal; follow KB5134907 instead of holding back DC updates.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source
